title: [Group Project] - Logic Gate
summary: Educational logic gate wiring simulator built with Qt and QGraphicsView

data.text: An educational logic gate wiring simulator where players learn how digital circuits work by connecting AND, OR, and NOT gates to solve 8 progressively harder puzzles. Built as a final group project for CS 3505 (Software Practice II) at the University of Utah with 5 contributors. I authored 100+ commits and was the primary developer for the core circuit system and game interaction layer.

items.content: Designed and implemented the Gate model with an enum-based type system (AND, OR, NOT, T, F, DOOR, C) and boolean evaluation logic that computes output from connected inputs
Built the Node model as connection endpoints for gates, supporting input/output roles, wire attachment/detachment, and null-safe pointer management
Implemented the Wire model for signal propagation between nodes, with color state toggling to visually reflect signal values (true/false)
Handled object lifecycle and memory management — fixed destructor ordering for gates, nodes, and wires to prevent dangling pointers and crashes from dynamic scene rearrangement
Built GateView using QGraphicsPixmapItem for rendering gate icons on the canvas with click-to-toggle behavior for T/F/C gates
Implemented WireView with real-time color updates reflecting signal propagation, click-to-delete, and edge case handling for reverse-connected and deleted wires
Created NodeView with mouse press/release event handling to initiate and complete wire connections between gates via temporary wire preview

Developed ToolView — a draggable gate palette using custom mouse event overrides (mousePressEvent, mouseMoveEvent, mouseReleaseEvent) for drag-and-drop from the tool panel onto the game canvas with 100px snap-to-slot positioning
Built MainWindow with QStackedWidget for page-based navigation between main menu, level select, and game views
Implemented level progression system — sequential level unlocking, timed challenges with fail-on-timeout, level completion detection, and auto-advance to next level
Added UI polish: styled level select buttons, help popup, toolbar layout, hover tooltips for gate descriptions, and warning messages for invalid wire connections
Integrated QMediaPlayer and QAudioOutput for title screen music and background audio
Resolved cross-platform mouse event handling differences between macOS and Windows — added event->accept() calls and refactored drag logic for consistent behavior
Wrote documentation for header files (gate.h, wire.h, wireview.h, mainwindow.h) using Doxygen-style comments
Managed merge conflicts and integration across 5 contributors working on concurrent features
Languages: C++
Frameworks: Qt 6, QGraphicsView, QGraphicsScene, QGraphicsPixmapItem, QStackedWidget, QMediaPlayer
Patterns: Model-View separation, Observer pattern (Qt signals/slots), enum-based type dispatch
Data Structures: Directed graph (nodes and edges for circuit wiring), std::vector for dynamic input management

Concepts: Object lifecycle and memory management (destructor ordering, dangling pointer prevention), event-driven programming, drag-and-drop with coordinate snapping, cross-platform input handling, boolean logic evaluation and signal propagation
Tools: Git (collaborative branching, merge conflict resolution), QMake, GitHub
